findings.finding: The second, independent viewport — the only discriminator the browser proof has against viewport-relative sizing — is absent from the VISUAL_COMPARE proof obligations' own `expected` statements. PROOF-b45848f515e94df8974e9605.expected is verbatim the Figma rule set for ELEMENT:4478:7209, whose observables both declare `viewports: [402]` only. The dual-viewport requirement (402x874 and 503x971) appears solely in change_item intent prose (CHG-4f40c7d947f91f32792b15db) and in implementation_constraints[3]; neither is the proof obligation an evaluator reads. A proof evaluated strictly against `expected` would measure at viewport 402 alone, where a frame styled `width:100%;height:100vh` renders at exactly 402x874 and passes. The plan is explicit that this must not pass — PROOF-bb3524ddaf253f025e9eaabd.expected states 'the separate independent browser VISUAL_COMPARE proof measures the exact fixed dimensions at both the required viewport and a second, different viewport' — so the obligation that is supposed to carry that discrimination does not state it. The Node markup check catches the literal strings '100%' and '100vh', but it is explicitly scoped to markup, not rendered geometry, and cannot catch equivalent constructs (external stylesheet, computed style, flex/absolute stretch) that produce viewport-relative geometry without those literals.

findings.finding: The preservation assertion prescribed by all three test obligations is not falsifiable and therefore cannot enforce its own stated failure condition. The obligation reads: "Execute an assertion that Screen.Existing is strictly equal to the Existing export of src/shared/ui/Existing.js; dropping the re-export must fail." Observed at revision 61b8634, src/shared/ui/Existing.js is `module.exports = {Existing: true};` — the preserved value is the boolean primitive `true`. Strict equality between two occurrences of the primitive `true` is satisfied regardless of provenance, so an implementation that deletes the require and writes `module.exports = {Existing: true}` (or any literal `true`) passes the assertion unchanged. The declared falsification condition ("dropping the re-export must fail") is thus unreachable by the prescribed check, and the only executable guard on the Screen.js re-export — which is inside write_scope and therefore mutable — is inert. Note that byte-for-byte preservation of src/shared/ui/Existing.js itself is independently enforced by boundaries.forbidden_policy=ALL_OUTSIDE_WRITE_SCOPE; the unguarded surface is specifically the re-export binding in src/features/example/Screen.js.

findings.required_correction: Replace the strict-equality clause in TEST-6fc8dd392b047354ec364dbc (and the identical clauses in TEST-7890e28269a6f67de26d3639 and TEST-bf46b224da5db8d06c659649) with a provenance-sensitive assertion that genuinely fails when the re-export is dropped. A sufficient formulation: clear the require cache for both modules, overwrite the cached export of src/shared/ui/Existing.js with a unique sentinel value (e.g. a fresh object `const S = {};`), re-require src/features/example/Screen.js, and assert by reference identity that Screen.Existing === S. A hardcoded literal in Screen.js fails this check, a live re-export passes it. Keep the existing value assertion as an additional check if desired, but it must not be the sole preservation guard.

findings.finding: The plan imposes two VISUAL_COMPARE proof obligations requiring rendered browser geometry at two viewports with both screenshots retained, but declares no owner, entry point, or evidence location for the observer that produces them, while forbidding every write outside two paths. boundaries.write_scope is limited to src/features/example/Screen.js and tests/ui.test.js with forbidden_policy ALL_OUTSIDE_WRITE_SCOPE, so the implementation cannot create a host page, harness, viewport driver, or screenshot sink. No candidate in the 185-row manifest is designated as the observer, and no path is given for the retained screenshots. The plan simultaneously asserts the observer is independent and that 'The code tested must never adjust the observer or its measurement' — consistent with the observer being external infrastructure — yet lists its output as a proof obligation of this delivery. The result is a genuine ownership ambiguity at the delivery boundary: an implementation agent cannot determine whether producing this evidence is its obligation, and the two available readings lead to materially different outcomes — either the delivery stalls on evidence it cannot generate, or the agent writes outside write_scope to generate it and trips the boundary. This is a gap in declaration, not in scope; the correction is a statement, not new work.

Either (a) state that the independent browser observer, its host page, its viewport driver and the screenshot deposit are supplied by the orchestration outside write_scope, require no implementer action, and that the implementation's sole obligation toward these proofs is to export the agreed entry point — in which case name that contract precisely (module src/features/example/Screen.js, named export `render`, zero arguments, returning an HTML string containing the frame and title elements); or (b) if the delivery must produce the evidence, add the observer path and the screenshot deposit path to boundaries.write_scope so the obligation is satisfiable within the declared boundary. Do not leave the proofs attached to the delivery with neither an owner nor a writable path.
